chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah said:

We entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Abu Basir asked him, 'What do you say about prayer in Ramadan?' He replied to him, 'Indeed, Ramadan has a sanctity and a right that is not like any of the other months. Pray as much as you can in Ramadan as voluntary prayer by night and by day. And if you can pray one thousand rak'ahs each day and night, then pray, for indeed Ali (peace be upon him) used to pray one thousand rak'ahs each day and night in the last period of his life. So pray, O Abu Muhammad, as an addition in Ramadan.'

He asked, 'How many? I am your ransom.' He said, 'For twenty nights, pass in each night twenty rak'ahs: eight rak'ahs before the 'Atamah (late night) prayer and twelve after it, besides what you used to pray before that. And when the last ten nights enter, pray thirty rak'ahs each night: eight before the 'Atamah and two and twenty after the 'Atamah, besides what you used to do before that.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific recommended voluntary prayers for the first twenty and last ten nights of Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific structure of night prayers (Qiyam) in Ramadan, distinguishing between the first twenty nights and the final ten nights, thereby establishing a jurisprudential basis for the 20-rak'ah Taraweeh practice in Shia tradition. It highlights the spiritual hierarchy of Ramadan by citing Imam Ali’s (AS) devotion in his final years as a model for increased voluntary worship. The text underscores the concept of 'Haqq' (due right) of the month, linking physical acts of worship to the unique sanctity that sets Ramadan apart from other months.
